statement: Says IdleOn is still worth playing after 2000 hours of active play; game is in early access with lots of potential.
His 2000-hour journey included crafting void armor, 16 megalodons, all W1-W2 achievements, building a guild, hardest bosses and party dungeons.
Late game becomes maintenance mode: daily duties, setting up 3D printer, post office, micromanaging construction, weeklies.
Daily duties include 3D printer to level alchemy bubbles, post office, construction micromanagement and weeklies.
Still plays actively and is excited waiting for new content despite maintenance mode.
Keeps grinding for highest AFK gains, maximum damage, and stacking skilling efficiency to get bigger 3D prints.
Game feels like RuneScape in grinding to 99 on every skill; it is more a self-set goal accomplishment.
After doing them so long, bosses and party dungeons feel like a chore, but are a very small part of the game.
He estimates the game is about a 50 split between idle and active play.
Gameplay is about accomplishing and increasing goals rather than having best gear; you can never cap out, an endless grind that can turn people off or hook them.
Name IdleOn undersells it; despite AFK games it is the least idle game he has played, with 2000 active and 42000 AFK hours.
With nine characters to control, he still hasn't completed everything and keeps working on the never-ending grind.
Likes no predatory microtransactions: special gem packs are flat rate and don't cost slightly more gems than lower packs to force bigger purchases.
You can get a ton of gems by playing the game and completing achievements.
Fears as new worlds are added the game could become overwhelming to many people due to all the skills classes and characters.
Characters are supposed to reach 12 eventually; only time will tell about the overwhelm issue.
Calls the MMO label a small issue: only party dungeons up to 10, guild perks, town chat; otherwise mostly solo.
Pixel art is appealing even after seeing it over and over.
Progressing from one world to the next doesn't make earlier worlds irrelevant unlike most RPGs.
He's far from done with the game, still has many self-goals and achievements to get, and says it is very playable after 2000 hours.
Some days are maintenance days spent micromanaging and min-maxing to be efficient; the game rewards efficiency over anything.
World 4 is coming out soon with lots more content to do and achieve.
